_meta.indication: FORZINITY is indicated to improve muscle strength in adult and pediatric patients with Barth syndrome weighing at least 30 kg.

pivotal_trials.phase: Barth syndrome clinical trial program (SPIBA-201 Part 1 randomized crossover; Part 2 open-label single-arm extension)
pivotal_trials.design: SPIBA-201, Part 1: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover with two 12-week treatment periods separated by a four-week washout; Part 2: open-label, single-arm, 192-week extension that enrolled 10 of the 12 subjects who completed Part 1.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Barth syndrome (BTHS) at least 12 years of age and weighing at least 30 kg.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint family in Part 1: distance walked on 6-minute walk test (6MWT) and total fatigue score (TFS) on the Barth syndrome symptom assessment. The accelerated-approval basis was the Part 2 secondary endpoint of knee extensor muscle strength by handheld dynamometry (HHD).
pivotal_trials.n: SPIBA-201 Part 1 randomized 12 subjects (N=12 elamipretide, N=12 placebo across crossover periods); 10 of the 12 continued into Part 2.
pivotal_trials.result: Part 1 was negative on the primary endpoint family (6MWT p=0.97; TFS p=0.89). In Part 2 (open-label), median change in HHD knee extensor strength (newtons) from pre-dose baseline was 34 at Week 12, 68 at Week 24, 57 at Week 36, 41 at Week 48, 35 at Week 72, and 64 at Week 168.

nct_ctgov.title: A Trial to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability and Efficacy of Elamipretide in Subjects With Barth Syndrome

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions are injection site reactions (any local administration reaction 100% elamipretide vs 67% placebo; injection site erythema 100% vs 25%). Serious hypersensitivity reactions requiring emergency medical intervention have occurred and require permanent discontinuation.
target_moa: Elamipretide localizes to and is enriched at the inner mitochondrial membrane (the site of abnormality in BTHS, where cardiolipin abnormalities from TAFAZZIN defects cause mitochondrial dysfunction), and is associated with improvements in mitochondrial structure and function.
modality: Peptide (small aromatic-cationic tetrapeptide; a mitochondrial cardiolipin binder administered by subcutaneous injection).

advisory_committee.vote: The Cardiovascular and Renal Drug Advisory Committee (CRDAC) met October 10, 2024 and voted 10 “Yes” and 6 “No” on whether elamipretide is effective for the treatment of Barth syndrome.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Knee extensor muscle strength assessed by handheld dynamometry (HHD) in SPIBA-201, Part 2, used as an intermediate clinical endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: the signatory authority has determined that the approach of accelerated approval for elamipretide based on the findings on knee extensor muscle strength assessed by HHD is a reasonable one for this very rare disease with high unmet need, accepting a somewhat greater risk (compared to a randomized trial) of false positive conclusions – and therefore less certainty about effectiveness

confirmatory_requirement.text: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients 5 years and older with Barth syndrome to verify and describe the clinical benefit predicted by improvements in knee extensor muscle strength assessed by HHD (PMR 4802-1).

orphan_indication.text: Elamipretide was granted Orphan Drug Designation (#DRU-2017-6078) for treatment of Barth syndrome on March 22, 2018.

summary.text: Elamipretide (Forzinity) received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 for Barth syndrome based on the intermediate endpoint of knee extensor muscle strength by HHD, after a prior Complete Response letter (May 15, 2025). It had orphan drug designation and priority review, an advisory committee (CRDAC) voted 10 Yes/6 No, and continued approval is contingent on a required confirmatory randomized controlled trial.

citations.quote: It is approved under accelerated approval pursuant to section 506(c) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) and 21 CFR 314.510, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling.
Elamipretide has orphan drug designation and received priority review.
The CRDAC vote was 10 “Yes” and 6 “No” on the question “Based on available evidence, do you conclude that elamipretide is effective for the treatment of Barth syndrome.”

basis.text: The effectiveness of elamipretide had not been established for traditional approval: SPIBA-201, Part 1 (the only randomized placebo-controlled study) did not show superiority on the primary endpoint family of 6MWT (p=0.97) and total fatigue score (p=0.89), and Part 2/SPIBA-001 could not overcome bias in effort-dependent endpoints; manufacturing facility deficiencies were also identified.

citations.quote: SPIBA-201, Part 1, the only randomized, placebo-controlled, study of elamipretide in patients with BTHS, did not show superiority of elamipretide to placebo on the primary endpoint family of distance walked on 6-minute walk test (6MWT) (p=0.97) and total fatigue score (TFS) on the Barth syndrome symptom assessment (p=0.89) at the end of the 12-week treatment period.
In addition, we identified deficiencies at the drug product manufacturing facility that will need to be resolved before this application can be approved.
